title: Bounded genus produces a model with rational singularities
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative normal Nagata local domain of dimension $2$ [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring], [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Suppose reduction to rational singularities is possible for $R$ [def-per-rational-surface-singularity]. Then there is a finite tower $X_n\to\cdots\to X_0=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of normalized blowups at closed points above the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. A normalized blowup means the blowup at the reduced closed point followed by normalization in its function field [def-nagata-global-blowup], [def-sc-normalization]. All the schemes $X_i$ are integral and normal, the normalizations in this tower are finite, and the composite $X_n\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is proper and induces an isomorphism of function fields [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-sc-function-field]. At every closed point $x\in X_n$ for which $\dim\mathcal O_{X_n,x}=2$, the local ring $\mathcal O_{X_n,x}$ defines a rational singularity. Length zero is allowed.

source.place: Tag 0B4P, resolve-lemma-reduce-to-rational; normalized point blowup convention Tag 0BBS, finiteness Tag 0BFT.

proof.text: By [def-per-rational-surface-singularity], the lengths $\ell_R H^1(M,\mathcal O_M)$ for normal modifications $M\to S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ belong to a bounded subset of $\mathbb N$. This subset is nonempty, since the identity of $S$ is a normal modification. A nonempty bounded subset of $\mathbb N$ has a largest element $L$; choose a normal modification $M$ attaining it. Here and below length has the meaning in [def-weil-pbc-module-length].

Apply [lem-per-nagata-surface-normalized-domination] to $M\to S$. Obtain its tower and write $T=T_n$ and $q:T\to M$. The exact sequence in [lem-per-surface-modification-h1-exact] for $T\to M\to S$, and length additivity [lem-weil-pbc-length-additive-short-exact], give $L\leq\ell_RH^1(T,\mathcal O_T)$. The reverse inequality holds because $T\to S$ is a normal modification and $L$ was maximal. Thus $T$ also attains $L$. This selects the same domination tower as the last paragraph of the source, before testing its local rings.

source.place: Tag 0B4P, first and third paragraphs; domination is taken before the local test.

proof.text: Let $g:Z\to T$ be any proper modification with $Z$ normal. The composite $Z\to S$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition], is integral and induces the composite isomorphism of function fields. Applying [lem-per-surface-modification-h1-exact] and [lem-weil-pbc-length-additive-short-exact] gives $$\ell_RH^1(Z,\mathcal O_Z)=L+\ell_RH^0(T,R^1g_*\mathcal O_Z).$$ The left side is at most $L$, so the last module has length zero. A nonzero module has the strict chain $0\subsetneq N$ and therefore positive length by [def-weil-pbc-module-length]; hence $H^0(T,R^1g_*\mathcal O_Z)=0$. The global generation assertion of [lem-per-surface-modification-h1-exact] now forces every stalk, and thus $R^1g_*\mathcal O_Z$, to vanish.

source.place: Tag 0B4P, first paragraph (maximality kills further first direct images).

proof.text: Fix a closed point $x\in T$ with $\dim B=2$, where $B=\mathcal O_{T,x}$. Normality of $T$ makes $B$ a normal local domain. By [lem-per-nagata-surface-normalized-domination], an affine neighbourhood of $x$ has a Nagata coordinate ring; its localization $B$ is Nagata by [lem-weil-pbc-nagata-localization], hence Noetherian. Let $h:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ be any normal modification, as in [def-per-rational-surface-singularity]. Each nonclosed point of the two-dimensional local spectrum has height zero or one. At height one the local ring is a DVR by [lem-sc-normal-dim1-dvr]. Thus [lem-per-normal-modification-codimension-one], clauses (1) and (2), shows that $h$ is an isomorphism on the punctured spectrum.

source.place: Tag 0B4P, second paragraph; resolve-situation-vanishing and its punctured-spectrum observation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-local-normal-modification-extension] to the normal Noetherian integral scheme $T$, its closed point $x$, and $h$. It gives a proper normal modification $g:Z\to T$ whose base change to $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is $h:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}B$. Its composite to $S$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition] and induces an isomorphism of function fields, so Step 3 applies and gives $R^1g_*\mathcal O_Z=0$.

source.place: Tag 0B4P, second paragraph, extension from the local spectrum via Tags 0B3X and 0BFN.

proof.text: The canonical map $a:\operatorname{Spec}B\to T$ is flat: on an affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}C$ of $x$ it is $C\to C_{\mathfrak p}$, and its local ring maps are localizations, which are flat by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat] and the stalkwise definition [def-weil-flat-morphism]. The proper map $g$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and its structure sheaf is quasi-coherent. Hence the sheaf form of [lem-pc-flat-base-change-cohom] gives $$R^1h_*\mathcal O_Y\cong a^*R^1g_*\mathcal O_Z=0.$$ For $h$ over the affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}B$, [lem-pc-affine-higher-direct-image-cohomology-vanishing] with $p=1,q=0$ gives $H^1(\operatorname{Spec}B,h_*\mathcal O_Y)=0$. The low degree exact sequence [pqf-lem-leray-lowdegree], with both this term and $H^0(\operatorname{Spec}B,R^1h_*\mathcal O_Y)$ zero, gives $H^1(Y,\mathcal O_Y)=0$. This writes out the source's final local-cohomology inference.

source.place: Tag 0B4P, second paragraph, last sentence, expanded using coherent.tex Tag 02KH and the affine-base Leray sequence.

proof.text: Since $h$ was arbitrary, [def-per-rational-surface-singularity] says that $B$ defines a rational singularity. This holds for every closed $x\in T$ of local dimension two. The tower chosen in Step 2 already has all the required normality, integrality, finite-normalization, properness, function-field and center properties by [lem-per-nagata-surface-normalized-domination]. Its length may be zero. Thus it is the asserted tower.

source.place: Tag 0B4P, conclusion, with the maximality argument on the dominating tower.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0B4P, resolve-lemma-reduce-to-rational; take the dominating normalized tower before applying the same maximality/localization argument to its closed points.

split_report.summary: Retained the existing statement and prior searches; fixed doubled TeX escapes. Followed 0B4P by a maximal H1-length normal modification and a dominating Nagata normalized point-blowup tower. The same exact sequence makes the tower maximal; globalization of arbitrary local modifications and explicit flat base change then prove its local rationality. Three statement-only subsidiary nodes; no excellence assumption added.

tool_uses.why: Affine-base vanishing at p=1,q=0 to finish local H1 vanishing.
The sheaf form of coherent flat base change in degree one, to localize the vanishing higher image.
Normal height-one local rings are DVRs for the punctured-spectrum test.
Length additivity for the maximality argument; the surface unit supplies no module-length theorem.
Flatness of the local-spectrum map used for coherent base change.
Nagata local rings on the tower; a generic localization tool.
Properness of the composite modification; a generic permanence tool.
The ordinary coherent low-degree Leray exact sequence; not an etale comparison.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q15-6fc988a11 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all three new nodes and every cited statement in full, and checked them against the source: Stacks resolve.tex 0B4N, 0B4P, 0BG0, 0AXF, situation-vanishing, 0BBS, 0BFT and 0BBT, and limits.tex 0B3X and 0BFN. The item statement is the same as the live unsplit node; only the TeX escapes changed. The dim-2 restriction on closed points was already there, so nothing is weakened. All 7 steps are sound. Steps 1-3: maximal H1 length, domination, and the 0AXF exact sequence plus length additivity, which show that the dominating tower T also attains the maximum L. Step 3 then gives R1g_*=0 for every normal modification of T, through the global-generation clause. Step 4: B is Nagata via the domination node and Nagata localization; primes below the maximal ideal have height at most 1; height-one rings are DVRs; codimension-one clauses (1),(2) make h an isomorphism on the punctured spectrum. Step 5: the 0B3X/0BFN extension Z->T. Step 6: flat base change, affine vanishing and low-degree Leray give H1(Y,O_Y)=0. Step 7 concludes. Dominating first avoids citing 0BG0 (unsplit), and this rearrangement is valid. New nodes are all true and match their sources. h1-exact is 0AXF; X' need not be normal, as in the source. local-normal-modification-extension is 0B3X+0BFN; normality comes from the local rings, integrality from the generic point; the Spec(field) edge case holds. nagata-surface-normalized-domination is 0BBT+0BFT with normal local base: X0=S, closed centers lie over the closed point, the normalizations are finite. Duplicate search: no existing 0AXF or 0B3X node. The excellent domination node needs a global excellent base and does not apply to a Nagata local ring, so it is not a duplicate. 0BG0 is neither cited nor restated. Batch-5 flag: lem-per-normal-modification-codimension-one reaches lem-trf-proper-finite-fibre-finite-near (Stacks 02UP: proper with finite fibre is finite near the point). That is a general morphism lemma that neither assumption provides and that is not specific to their proofs, so I accept the citation. No SGA citations. Tool_uses (all generic) are accepted. No fixes.
